figures.caption: Fig. 1. Overview and motivation of NEURONS++. (a) Existing approaches often rely on implicit latent-space alignment or independently aggregated visual cues, leaving the neural-to-visual hierarchy weakly structured. (b) NEURONS++ connects static and dynamic reconstruction through a visual-stream formulation and progressively transforms neural activity into structured visual cues through a brain-inspired Serial Visual Decoupler. (c) Delta-fMRI perturbation, ROI ablation, and ROI amplification provide evidence of directional controllability, stimulus-relevant cortical sensitivity, and region-selective semantic modulation.

Fig. 2. Overall framework of NEURONS++. The brain encoding module maps fMRI voxels into visual and textual embeddings aligned with foundationmodel spaces. NEURONS++ is trained through multi-subject pretraining (MSP) on image-fMRI data and subject-specific adaptation (SSA) on target image or video datasets. The Serial Visual Decoupler progressively decodes explicit visual cues through four stages: key object segmentation, concept recognition, scene description, and blurry visual-stream reconstruction. During inference, these decoded cues condition an unCLIP-based keyframe reconstruction process, followed by either a pretrained image-to-image diffusion model for image reconstruction or a pretrained text-to-video diffusion model for video reconstruction.

Fig. 3. Overview of the conference version NEURONS [18]. In this journal version, we inherit the decoupled task construction while extending the setting from video-only reconstruction to visual-stream reconstruction and the architecture from parallel task aggregation to serial visual decoding.

Fig. 6. Qualitative comparison of fMRI-to-image reconstruction on NSD. Each pair shows the ground-truth image and the NEURONS++ reconstruction.

Fig. 8. Per-sample stimulus specificity of ROI causal dependence. For each test sample, the ROI ablation profile (∆cos across the eight ROIs) is correlated by Spearman’s ρ with the sample’s own fMRI ROI activation-energy profile (matched, red) or with that of a randomly paired sample (mismatched, blue). A higher ρ indicates that the encoder relies most on the ROIs that the stimulus most strongly drives.

Fig. 10. Model attribution maps match real cortical activation energy. From left to right: the stimulus frame, the model attribution map projected onto the cortical surface, and the real fMRI ROI activation energy. For a face stimulus, the model highlights face-selective regions; for a scene stimulus, the attribution shifts toward place-selective regions.

Fig. 11. Matched semantic lift and asymmetric double dissociation under targeted ROI boosting. (A) Bar plots show CLIP-face and CLIP-place scores before and after boosting the corresponding ROI. Each boost selectively elevates the semantic score matched to its known functional role. (B) Bars display the change (∆) in semantic scores when boosting the face ROI or the place ROI. Targeted boosting enhances its matched semantic score while suppressing the competing category’s score.

Fig. 12. Boosting functional ROIs steers decoded content toward the matched category. Each column shows one example stimulus; rows show the ground-truth frame, the unmanipulated reconstruction, the face-ROI-boosted reconstruction, and the place-ROI-boosted reconstruction.
